text:
maria: Heads up — noticed steady KV residency growth on the on-prem A100 pool when handling long-context sessions (>20k tokens). Dedicated and Hosted traces look different.
aj: do you have a short repro or profile?
maria: minimal repro attached, but quick perf sample:
```
# perf top snippet (summary)
samples  : 120K of 1M cycles
kv_cache_reclaim                42.1%  (hot)
page_return_handler             18.7%
cuda_memcpy_async               12.3%
jemalloc_arena_ctl              8.4%
fallback_generic_attention      6.1%
```
maria: on on-prem we see reclaim + page_return dominating; on Hosted the hotspot is memcpy and kernel-selection stalls, not reclaim.
olga: interesting — what's the kernel selection path? are we falling back to the generic attention kernel on-prem?
maria: yes, for long sequences the runtime picks an alternative attention tiling we use in on-prem builds (tuned for A100/driver X.Y). that path pins frames and seems to prevent timely page-return, leading to fragmentation + slow reclaim.
leo: could be NUMA/hugepage differences too. on Dedicated we enable 2MB hugepages and different jemalloc config; Hosted uses default.
sam: also check batching_window_ms — longer windows push bigger KV pages, makes reuse higher but increases residency. what's current?
maria: batching_window_ms=7ms for on-prem workload, 3ms for Hosted. trying 3ms locally reduced peak by ~14% in quick test.
aj: VPC constraints — any MTU/network stuff causing extra copies? infra-bot: note: VPC path has 1500 MTU, on-prem rack uses 9000. large RPC frames get segmented differently, might change kernel routing heuristics.
olga: that could change how we choose between GPUDirect vs staged memcpy. if kernel selection prefers staged memcpy it increases host pinned buffers lifetime -> more KV residency on host.
maria: exact behavior: on-prem -> GPUDirect path used but combined with our custom attention kernel that retains KV pageframes pinned across requests. Dedicated with hugepages avoids pagefaults, Hosted with smaller batches triggers kernel fallback earlier so pages are evicted sooner. weirdly both are bad in different ways.
sam: any perf regressions correlate to a rollout? last week we switched kernel build flags (AVX512 -> generic) for regression fix.
maria: timestamped around 2950008000 we deployed a kernel tweak. regression window matches.
leo: quick experiment: switch jemalloc background_thread=1 and reduce arena_decay to 30s, see if reclaim latency drops. sam: I'll try a canary with batch_window=3ms + jemalloc background.
aj: can we add a small heatmap profile from the runtime for KV slot residency vs token position? that helped earlier.
qa-bot: reminder: add a short test to long-context perf job to catch >10% growth over 6h.
olga: also run `nvprof --samples` on on-prem to see NVLink stalls and page faults. Maria, can you share the repro command?
maria: repro (short):
```
./run_infer --model t5-xl --seq_len 22k --batch 1 --profile=kv_residency --runtime-opts "batching_window_ms=7"
```
maria: plan: 1) run nvprof and perf on on-prem (olga+sam), 2) try batching_window_ms=3 and jemalloc tweaks on a canary (sam), 3) if that helps, add automatic policy: lower batching when longctx user detected; otherwise keep aggressive batching for throughput.
aj: SG. assign owners and timeline?
maria: olga/sam run experiments today. leo to validate hugepage vs no-hugepage delta. I'll post aggregated flame/heatmap by EOD.
olga: started nvprof capture on node-7. will post artifacts to /infra/perf/2950014100/
sam: kicking off canary now with jemalloc+batching change. will update within 2hrs. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
aj: if we find kernel-selection is the root cause we should consider a small runtime flag to prefer eviction-friendly kernels for longctx flows.
maria: agreed. even a per-tenant flag for Dedicated/private would help.
leo: note for release engineers — any kernel ABI change we apply to on-prem must also be reflected on Dedicated images to avoid config drift.
infra-bot: deploy-canary started for sam's run (canary-id: c-2950014210).
qa-bot: test job queued: longctx-regression-check.
aj: thanks all — keep updates here and attach profiles. :thumbsup:
